args: In libxml2/HTMLparser.c, analyze all endDocument callback dispatches in htmlParseDocument (around lines 4956-5057), htmlParseTryOrFinish (around lines 5572, 5790, and 6237), and htmlParseChunk (around line 6325). Which dispatches can occur after fatal errors set ctxt->disableSAX, and what minimal root-cause fix is consistent with the parser's SAX dispatch policy? Also note whether skipping endDocument when disableSAX is set could disrupt parser state transitions.

The reported PoV causes an allocation failure during encoding conversion in pull parsing. htmlParseDocument begins with a guarded startDocument callback, but its final endDocument callback checks only ctxt->sax and the callback pointer. The OOM path sets ctxt->disableSAX=1, input cursors may point to an empty global sentinel, and default SAX2 endDocument accesses unsafe aborted-context metadata, producing a global-buffer-overflow at line 5057. I suspect the direct fix is adding !ctxt->disableSAX to the final callback guard, but I am checking analogous push-parser dispatches to ensure the root policy is applied correctly and no state update depends on the callback.
